issues.label: Agent-native semantic GPU debugger and profiler
Deterministic CPU semantic simulator and virtual GPU runtime

capabilities.label: Rust ownership and result flow
capabilities.detail: rustc remains the only Rust borrow checker: it enforces moves, borrows, lifetimes, visibility, and local typestate. Fe2O3 extends those rules with sealed non-Clone GPU capabilities and workload-neutral cross-invocation verification. Typed kernels may return KernelResult and use ?, while the macro emits a private unit-ABI entry wrapper and the compiler retains the helper's real MIR. Err ends only the current invocation and is not a host-visible error channel.

capabilities.label: Pliron context ownership
capabilities.detail: Process-local context identities, registered dialects, and context-bound handles are checked before operations are inspected. Generic safety passes execute today; issue #140 tracks stronger owner-aware upstream arena handles rather than blocking the production verifier sequence.

capabilities.label: Generic pre-lowering safety
capabilities.detail: The mandatory workload-neutral sequence verifies tensor layout and collective participation, ranked bounds, atomic legality, cross-invocation race freedom, barrier convergence, workgroup-memory initialization and publication, and declared semantic refinement. It reasons per subgroup, wave, workgroup, and grid where the execution contract provides authority. Rejected and Incomplete findings both stop strict production compilation before lowering.

capabilities.label: Rust production route
capabilities.detail: Ordinary safe Rust reaches semantic MIR, ranked PLIRON verification, canonical Kernel IR V7, formal memory admission, gfx942 LLVM, HSACO, and qualification launch for dynamic strided GEMM, row softmax, fused attention, and grouped-expert MoE. The kernels use native Result control flow, target-neutral Matrix, Subgroup, and Math capabilities, runtime dimensions, compiler-guarded edge loads, dynamic loops, additive masks, tiled disjoint outputs, and epilogues through one workload-neutral route. Unsupported effects and ownership forms remain deliberately fail-closed.

capabilities.label: Bounded compiler analysis
capabilities.detail: Closed control-flow validation, pruned SSA placement, block-argument uniformity, sparse index facts, dynamic tiled-component reasoning, subgroup-scoped bounded invocation traces, Result and Option payload dominance, and stable diagnostics feed every workload through the same safety pipeline. Bounded unsigned range facts propagate through add, subtract, divide, remainder, equality, and ordering guards only while exact CFG dominance and mutation analysis keep them valid; address escape or an unresolved write disables the proof. Checked add, subtract, and multiply retain value plus overflow through canonical KIR V7. Typed matrix producers retain operand role, profile, register distribution, storage provenance, wave association, and zero-fill policy without naming algorithms. Unsupported operations and resource limits fail closed as Incomplete obligations.

capabilities.label: Target finalization
capabilities.detail: The current qualification route emits gfx942 LLVM, links HSACO, loads it through fe2o3-host, and checks dynamic GEMM, row-softmax, fused-attention, and grouped-expert GPU results against independent CPU references. Disassembly confirms MFMA for matrix contractions and lane shuffles for reductions. The published measurements are correctness qualifications; only the GEMM lesson includes a matched direct HIP comparison, and it does not claim a speed advantage. Protected release authority and complete source-to-machine refinement remain separate.

capabilities.label: Runtime and persistent execution
capabilities.detail: Pure-Rust KFD topology, memory, queue, packet, and typed lifecycle foundations are present. The direct-KFD semantic observation boundary does not dispatch work: its redacted report exposes queue-lifecycle and resource facts only, with no dispatch identity, timing, KIR, workgroup, wave, lane, memory, or register observation. Authority-free Worker V2 crash-recovery mechanics remain separate. These records grant no publication, load, or launch authority; verified persistent execution and complete production runtime authority remain open in issues #135 and #137.

capabilities.label: Semantic debugging and profiling
capabilities.detail: Versioned semantic trace records, deterministic bounded hierarchy queries, and import boundaries establish an agent-readable foundation. The importer can retain selected rocprofv3 JSON dispatch-envelope and timing observations, ATT manifest metadata without decoded events, and sparse normalized ROCgdb records with explicit unavailable fields. There is no debugger or profiler UI, general source/MIR/KIR/ISA map, counter or PC-sample ingestion, ATT decoding, structured ROCgdb state, capture comparison, or diagnosis authority yet. Issue #215 tracks those layers.

capabilities.label: No-GPU CPU semantic simulation
capabilities.detail: cargo fe2o3 simulate can take ordinary typed source through semantic MIR, verified canonical Kernel IR V7, formal-memory admission, and bounded deterministic CPU execution. The fe2o3 path links and initializes no GPU runtime and performs no GPU enumeration; ordinary project Cargo build scripts remain trusted, unsandboxed host code outside that claim. The current slice covers structured scalar control flow and internal calls, private and global buffers or views, ordinary and guarded scalar loads, D1-D3 invocation identities, static scalar workgroup memory, and convergent workgroup barriers under one cooperative canonical schedule. The result includes copied buffers and a bounded byte-level cross-invocation conflict assessment; a separate adapter can emit observation-only semantic traces. It grants no race-freedom proof, source-to-KIR or GPU equivalence, launch authority, timing, or performance prediction. Floating point, MFMA and wave operations, atomics and fences, dynamic or non-scalar workgroup memory, external calls, memory intrinsics, inline assembly, schedule exploration, and a virtual host runtime remain open in issue #216.
